current_paragraph_excerpt: Universities govern faculty inventions through written policy. Intellectual-property policies specify who owns inventions, when they must be disclosed, how rights are assigned, and how licensing revenue is shared. Research on university patenting, licensing, and technology-transfer offices has examined these arrangements from several angles \citep{mowery2001growth,sampat2006patenting,jensen2003disclosure,ouellette2020patent}. A related literature studies academics' wider engagement with industry, which extends beyond licensing \citep{perkmann2021academic}. Even a prominent policy provision, the inventor's royalty share, has proven difficult to link reliably to commercialization: the positive association between royalty shares and licensing income reported by \citet{lach2008incentives} was subsequently challenged by \citet{ouellette2020patent}, who identified errors in the earlier coding and found no compelling evidence of a robust effect. Coding the terms of a policy may capture only part of what the policy conveys. The same disclosure or assignment rule can be written as a command or as an offer of assistance. This paper measures that second dimension in the written policies. It does not estimate its effects on inventor behavior

current_paragraph_excerpt: We construct the Policy Communication Stance Index (PCSI) from intellectual-property policies at 150 U.S.\ research universities over 1944--2025. The corpus contains 518 source-document records and 87,159 cleaned sentences, which yield 480 university-years with policy text and 4,277 annual policy-in-force observations. Human-coded sentences define restrictive, neutral, and supportive communication; a fine-tuned contextual classifier\footnote{A contextual classifier uses the words around a phrase when deciding its meaning. Fine-tuning means adapting a previously trained language model to the sentences labeled for this study.} scales those judgments to the full corpus; and calibrated class probabilities are aggregated to the university-year level. The approach follows the text-as-data literature's emphasis on defining the construct before scaling it statistically \citep{grimmer2013text,gentzkow2019text,adcock2001measurement}.

current_paragraph_excerpt: The communicative-constitution view of organizations holds that organizations exist in and through communication, and that written texts are able to circulate beyond the setting in which they were written. current_paragraph_excerpt: Institutional rules state what people are required or allowed to do. Yet the same rule can also suggest how an institution expects to relate to the people it governs \citep{crawford1995grammar,phillips2004discourse}. The Institutional Grammar describes institutional statements through five elements: who is addressed, the obligation or permission, the action, the conditions, and any consequence for noncompliance \citep{crawford1995grammar}. We study the language used to express those expectations. It is the part of a policy that tells inventors whether they are addressed as subjects of institutional control or as partners whom the institution will assist, and it can vary while the regulative content stays fixed. The distinction motivates three propositions about the texts, distinct from any claim about how inventors respond to them.

current_paragraph_excerpt: Institutional rules state what people are required or allowed to do. Yet the same rule can also suggest how an institution expects to relate to the people it governs \citep{crawford1995grammar,phillips2004discourse}. The Institutional Grammar describes institutional statements through five elements: who is addressed, the obligation or permission, the action, the conditions, and any consequence for noncompliance \citep{crawford1995grammar}. We study the language used to express those expectations. It is the part of a policy that tells inventors whether they are addressed as subjects of institutional control or as partners whom the institution will assist, and it can vary while the regulative content stays fixed. The distinction motivates three propositions about the texts, distinct from any claim about how inventors respond to them.

current_paragraph_excerpt: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{P\arabic*.},leftmargin=2.2em,itemsep=2pt] \item \textbf{Separability.} If framing is distinct from regulative content, stance should vary substantially among sentences with the same rule form, and a stance measure should not reduce to counts of obligations, prohibitions, and sanctions. \item \textbf{Institutional persistence.} Texts become institutionalized when they are produced by actors with legitimate authority and are drawn on repeatedly by others \citep{phillips2004discourse}; studies of contracts suggest that formal language can be copied and changed incrementally, leaving traces of earlier drafts \citep{kahan1997standardization,choi2013dynamics}. Stance should therefore be a persistent, organization-specific attribute that broad organizational categories predict only weakly. \item \textbf{Field-level drift.} Organizations in the same field can respond to shared legal and professional pressures and adopt similar forms \citep{dimaggio1983iron,edelman1992legal}. If such pressures change the register in which universities write, we would expect changes across multiple universities and parts of their policies, not only in the clauses that a particular legal event touches. \end{enumerate}

current_paragraph_excerpt: The preserved labeled sample contains 2,732 sentences: 2,458 for training and 274 held out for validation. The model metadata reports 90.1 percent accuracy and 0.894 macro-F1 on a held-out validation set; these historical training-run metrics have not been independently re-estimated because the original labeled records were not retained.\footnote{Accuracy is the fraction of held-out sentences whose predicted class matches its human label. Precision is the share of a class's predictions that are correct, and recall is the share of that class's actual sentences recovered. The F1 statistic is their harmonic mean. Macro-F1 averages the three class-specific F1 scores equally, so a common class cannot dominate the statistic.} The model returns a probability distribution over restrictive, neutral, and supportive stance for every sentence, and we apply post-hoc temperature scaling\footnote{Temperature scaling adjusts a model's reported probabilities using a single fitted parameter. It does not change which class has the highest score.} before aggregation \citep{guo2017calibration}. Appendix~\ref{app:model} reports the configuration and calibration parameter.

current_paragraph_excerpt: \paragraph{Where the variation lies.} In the annual policy-in-force panel, 61.0 percent of the total sum of squared deviations in PCSI is between universities and 39.0 percent is within universities over time. Because the panel repeats a score until a newer source appears, carry-forward mechanically increases persistence; using only the 480 source-text university-years lowers the between-university share to 48.7 percent (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:variance}). Carry-forward matters for the magnitude, but it does not create the cross-university structure. Revisions are typically incremental: across 330 consecutive policy revisions within universities, the median absolute change in PCSI is 0.021. The pattern resembles a stable institutional writing style. This is an analogy to the persistent differences found in other organizational settings, not direct evidence about the people who drafted these policies \citep[compare][]{bertrand2003managing}.

Studies of corporate contracts and sovereign bonds find that legal language is often carried over and adapted from earlier documents \citep{kahan1997standardization,choi2013dynamics}. Shared legal and professional pressures could help explain the shift toward more restrictive wording \citep{dimaggio1983iron,edelman1992legal}; the evidence of drift within several keyword-defined clause topics and rule forms is consistent with a change in drafting register. The exact descriptive decompositions attribute most of the modern decline to within-category changes under the chosen definitions; they do not establish that the underlying legal content was unchanged or identify causal drivers. The institutional results fit the broader technology-transfer literature, which emphasizes heterogeneous professional routines, faculty--TTO relationships, and local commercialization practices \citep{owensmith2001patent,siegel2003assessing,bercovitz2008academic,perkmann2021academic}.
